title: From Item NFA to LR(0) DFA via Subset Construction
description: Build the item NFA for a grammar and apply epsilon-closure and subset construction to obtain the LR(0) DFA states and transitions.

steps.description: Define PRODS and NONTERMINALS, enumerate all 11 (production, dot position) pairs in ITEMS, and write show(item) to display the dot.
In edges(item), add a transition on rhs[d] to (p, d + 1), plus 'eps' transitions to every production of rhs[d] when rhs[d] is a nonterminal.

steps.question: What arrows does edges((1, 0)) produce for item i2: S -> . X y x?
steps.answer: Because the dot sits before nonterminal X, it produces a symbol arrow ('X', (1, 1)) to i3 and two epsilon arrows ('eps', (2, 0)) and ('eps', (3, 0)) to i6 and i9.

steps.description: Implement eps_closure(states) using a frontier worklist that follows 'eps' edges, and move(states, symbol) to step across a grammar symbol.
Run the subset construction starting from start = eps_closure({(0, 0)}), computing move(S, symbol) followed by eps_closure(T) for each DFA state, then print all states and arrows.
Inspect result at the end of eps_closure({(0, 0)}) to see DFA state 0 containing items i0, i2, i6, and i9.
